title: Find the Hidden Word (DFS + Backtracking on Grid)
real_world_story: A word-puzzle game hides a secret word on a letter board. The player traces the word through neighboring tiles without lifting the finger from any tile twice, and the game must verify the trace instantly.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Letter board where each cell is a tile
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Starting DFS from every matching tile and undoing each step to try the next neighbor

problem_statement: Given an R x C board of uppercase letters and a word W, determine whether W can be formed by starting at any cell and moving 4-directionally (up, down, left, right). The same cell may not be used more than once in the word path.
task: Return 1 if the word exists on the board, otherwise 0.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain a string of C uppercase letters. The final line contains the word W.
output_format: Print 1 if the word exists, otherwise 0.
constraints: Board and word contain only A-Z

examples.explanation: ABCB cannot be traced without reusing a cell.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Each trace is a depth-first path with visited marking and undo, exploring neighbors until the full word is matched.

complexity.time: O(R * C * 4^L) worst case where L is word length

hint: Start DFS from every cell matching the first letter.
Mark a cell visited before recursing and unmark it afterward.
Return true as soon as the last letter is matched.
real_world_takeaway: DFS with backtracking verifies word traces on puzzle grids without revisiting tiles.
